key_insight: The paper reframes 3D image editing from vague conditioning to explicit geometry: instead of saying where an object should roughly be, the user specifies both its input and output 3D boxes. This makes large spatial edits and camera changes easier to control in real images.
problem_solved: Text prompts and 2D conditioning often fail to precisely control spatial transformations, especially when objects move far or the viewpoint changes. Existing 3D box methods mostly provide coarse location cues rather than a clear description of the desired edit.
method: Represent the edit using structured 3D boxes that define both the starting and target object geometry.
Treat editing as a well-posed geometric transformation problem rather than an ambiguous semantic instruction.
Use the box specification to guide realistic image editing under large motion and viewpoint change.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more interpretable and controllable interface for real-image editing. It can improve reliability in applications where precise object relocation, pose change, or camera-aware edits are needed.

paper_title: Thinking in Boxes: 3D Editing in Real Images Made Easy
paper_authors: Pradhaan S Bhat, Naveen Chandra R, Rishubh Parihar, Vaibhav Vavilala, R. Venkatesh Babu
